Rust · eframe and egui · no embedded browser
Every piece of the program and how it talks to the next: the interface, the engine, the vault, Windows, the seven platforms, and your encrypted data folder
solid: files moving on your machine · dashed: a read or a query · gold numbers point into the screenshot beside them
Steam, Battle.net, Riot, Epic, Ubisoft, Rockstar and GOG.

Only three interfaces: the registry to find where platforms

It runs as an ordinary user.

A three-layer hexagon with two turning arcs and a scanning line. The lock
at its centre stays green while the vault is open
Vault state, the cipher in use, that the key is bound to this machine, and
that nothing is tracked. Four facts, not promises
How many accounts you have saved, how many of the seven platforms were
found installed, and the active profile's name
Each platform with its own colour and account count, and a green dot when
it is installed. Clicking one opens its accounts
Home, then the seven platforms, then team and settings. Keys 1 to 7 move
you between them from the keyboard
It changes every six and a half seconds and explains one piece at a time.
You can switch it off in settings
Always shown at the bottom so you never have to memorise them: Esc closes,
digits jump to platforms, S opens settings, L locks the vault
